2. Plaintiff opposite party instituted Title Suit No. 4 and 5 of 2011 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for the remedies :— 

 3. It is stated in the plaint that plaintiff participated in the tender for construction of multi-storied commercial-cum car parking building within the area of Gulshan-(South) and Gushan-2 (North), Dhaka under Dhaka City Corporation of which tender was floated in different newspapers from 25-11-2009 up to 5-12-2009. Plaintiff submitted his tender with all required papers on 2-2-2010 and also deposited Taka 100 (One hundred) crore as financial bid security certificate. Plaintiff through national and international consultant for drawing architectural plan, elevation, structural design, drawing and estimate etc. expend Taka 77,00,0000 and fulfilled all the requirement of Dhaka City Corporation, submitted tender. Plaintiff also submitted as per clause 20.1 (b)(II) certificate for working capital. As per terms of that tender Taka 15(fifteen) crore was required but plaintiff has credit facilities to the tune of Taka 23.31 crore. Moreover, the banker of plaintiff, National Bank Ltd. issued further Financial Security Certificate to the tune of Taka 100 crore. Plaintiff also deposited original certificate along with tender Form. It is learnt that Dhaka City Corporation with mala fide intention will evaluate the tender bid of plaintiff as non-responsive. Plaintiff moved the Hon'ble Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development and Co-operatives on 8-4-2010. Senior Assistant Secretary of the aforesaid Ministry issued letter to the Mayor, Dhaka City Corporation on 21-4-2010. Plaintiff also issued two letters dated 6-4-2010 and 25-12-2010 for changing his status as responsive but having not received any response from Mayor, Dhaka City Corporation, filed the suit. 

 4. Along with plaint, plaintiff filed application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying as follows:— 

 5. Learned Judge on 4-1-2011 issued show cause notice upon the defendants. On 9-1-2011 plaintiff filed application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for an order of injunction so that defendants may not open financial offers of bidders and may not issue any work order. Learned Judge on that date (i.e. 9-1-11) directed the parties to maintain 'strictly status quo'. On 27-1-2011 after hearing the parties, by the impugned order, granted injunction findings that plaintiff has prima facie case for injunction, plaintiff was found to be responsive in the 1st meeting of the tender committee and if injunction be not granted then plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss which cannot compensated by any means. 

 7. It is further required to be consider that earlier also this matter came before this Court and a Division Bench of this Court issued Rule in Civil Revision No. 170 of 2011. It is also stated that plaintiff earlier moved before the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in Writ jurisdiction in Writ Petition Nos. 2791 of 2010, 2793 of 2010 and 2794 of 2010 which was disposed of on 11-4-2010, against which, Dhaka City Corporation preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 834-836 of 2010 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division and the Appellate Division by order dated 31-5-2010 dismissed the aforesaid leave petitions but directed Dhaka City Corporation to proceed with the tender process in accordance with law. 

 8. Mr AJ Mohammad AIi learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant, submits that, relief sought for in the suit under law cannot be granted as such, suit is not maintainable and since suit is hit under section 42 of the Special Relief Act, no injunction on such suit can be granted forestall development work taken by defendant appellant. Learned Advocate further submits that, order passed by the learned Judge is violatative to the order passed by the Appellate Division while dismissing Civil Petition Nos. 834-836 of 2010 directing the defendant appellant to proceed with the tender process. Learned Advocate further submits that order of injunction as granted should be interfered as by this injunction order the development work taken by the Dhaka City Corporation has been delayed and no Court should restrain Government to frustrate its development project. Learned Advocate further submits that as per Section 21 of Public Procurement Act, 2006 and Public Procurement Rules, 2008 plaintiff has remedy before the authority as Part 2 in section 41, sections 47, 48, 51 and 52 and also in part 4 in section 60 and also in chapter 7 in section 64 and in chapter 9 in section 66 provide opportunity to plaintiff to redress his grievance if any, but this suit having been filed without exhausting the aforesaid provision of law, the suit is not maintainable, consequently no injunction can be granted. 

 9. Mr TH Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff opposite party, on the other hand, submits that, gross illegality have done to the plaintiff by treating his offer at first responsive, later non-responsive without hearing the plaintiff by which it is clear that plaintiff will not get any justice if plaintiff invoke the provisions of Public Procurement Act, 2006 and Rules, 2008 and the plaintiff having no other alternative, filed the suit which is maintainable and injunction as granted thus sustainable in law. Learned Advocate further Submits that since this Court did not pass interlocutory order while admitting the appeal and injunction order is continuing from 21-3-2011 and by this time 4 months the injunction order is continuing, said order should not be disturbed: 

 10. In this appeals; Joint Venture Consortium (JVCA) of Borak Real Estate Pvt. Ltd and Unique Hotel and Resources Ltd represented by Mohammad Noor Ali, Member-in-Charge filed application for being added as a party stating that applicant and plaintiff having on the same footing as applicant participated in the tender bid along with plaintiff, as such, he has interest in disposal of the suit and should be added in the proceeding: 

 12. On the question of validity of injunction order. It is true that there is provision in Public Procurement Act, 2006 that before moving Court one should exhaust the provisions mentioned herein before but on a reading to the aforesaid sections and rules we find there is no provision raising bar to file suit and suit will fail for non compliance of the aforesaid laws. Learned Judge granted injunction considering that plaintiff make out a prima facie arguable case and balance of inconvenience is in favour of the plaintiff. In these appeals trial Court granted injunction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as such, we should not propose to step into the controversy as to whether in the instant case the application for temporary injunction satisfy the requirements of Order XXXIX, rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Reference may be make to the decision of Abdul Jalil Munshi vs Abu Bakar Siddique, 35 DLR (AD) 42. 

 I) the application has a prima facie case to go to trial, 

 i) applicant must show a fair prima facie case in support of the right claimed ; 

 15. On a reading of the impugned order it appears that learned Judge at least satisfied that there is prima facie case for granting injunction. 

 16. In the case of Mia Mohammad Latif vs Province of West Pakistan, 22 DLR (SC) 98 prima facie case for granting temporary injunction defined as: 

 "In a case where temporary injunction is claimed the plaintiff has only to make out that he has a good prima facie case making thereby that an important question of law is to be tried in the suit and that in the event of success if the injunction is not issued he will suffer irreparable injury." 

 17. 'Irreparable injury' means only that injury which cannot be compensated. The plaintiff in his plaint has made out a case that how he was treated mala fide, by the defendants and unless the defendants be restrained, the work order if issued to a 3rd party then he will be remediless.
